Hi Emily (and MedWise security team),

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the call and the clear context on your use case. Quick recap and next steps so we can keep momentum.

Recap (what we heard):
- MedWise plans to use LLMs to power clinical summarization and patient message triage; PHI will be present in requests and stored results.
- Security and procurement want: 1) BAA availability, 2) clear boundaries for PHI processing, 3) evidence (SOC 2 Type II), and 4) an initial vendor security questionnaire.

How Redwood supports HIPAA workloads (summary):
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) — eligible for PHI with a signed BAA. Provides dedicated GPU pools, network isolation, and can be deployed with customer VPC connectivity. Recommended for predictable throughput + PHI.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — eligible for PHI with BAA. Best for regulated / air-gapped requirements; customer controls networking and keys.
- Hosted (multi-tenant API) — not recommended for PHI by default. We can discuss limited hosted scenarios, but default guidance: do not send PHI over our shared hosted endpoints unless explicitly scoped and with additional controls.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm that you will be sending PHI and that MedWise requires a BAA (yes/no).
2) Security: can you have someone on security/security@medwisehealth.com fill out the attached vendor questionnaire?
3) Procurement: I'll attach a draft BAA for initial review (we can route via DocuSign once legal is aligned).
4) If helpful, we propose a technical sync with our security engineering lead (Dev) to walk through network/KMS/audit details — propose Tue 7/20 10:00am PT or Wed 7/21 2:00pm PT.

On Thu, Jul 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap (what we heard):
> - MedWise plans to use LLMs to power clinical summarization and patient message triage; PHI will be present in requests and stored results.

Thanks for the context — tagging in a few engineering points we should surface to the customer. Feel free to paste these back to Emily/security:

High-level: Redwood can sign a BAA for dedicated and private deployment options. Hosted multi-tenant endpoints are not covered for PHI by default. Details below.

Technical boundaries / capabilities:
- BAA: Available for Dedicated and Private deployments. We have an established BAA template (attached by Marissa). Typical legal review time ~3–5 business days; DocuSign turnaround after redlines ~1–2 business days.
- SOC 2: We maintain a SOC 2 Type II report; we can provide a downloadable copy under NDA or via a secure share.
- Audit logs: Per-request audit logs with timestamp, request id, model + version, and token counts. Logs can be exported to customer S3 buckets or forwarded to a customer SIEM via syslog or cloud-native integrations. Retention configurable per contract (default 90 days, can extend).
- KMS / encryption: Support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private deployments; encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3) and encryption at rest.
- Data residency: Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in the customer's cloud region (US/EU/APAC variants) to help with data residency requirements. Private on-prem deployment offers full control.
- PHI handling guidance: Do not route PHI through hosted multi-tenant API. For initial pilots we recommend Dedicated with VPC peering and prefix/KV caching disabled for PHI-sensitive routes until validated.

Open items for legal/security:
- Confirm desired audit log retention and delivery method (S3 push vs. webhook/syslog).
- Any additional encryption/HSM certifications required? (FIPS, HSM vendor)

If you want, I can join Tue 7/20 10:00am PT to walk through network diagrams and key rotation details.
